comparison: Both strongly support TRMT1 cleavage by Mpro (C29-C39). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from western blots with two antibodies and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers praise the convincing demonstration using both recombinant and endogenous TRMT1, with Reviewer 2 highlighting the use of C145A inactive variant and dual antibody approach.

Both support functional consequences of cleavage (C40-C43, C49-C50). OpenEval focuses on methyltransferase activity and EMSA binding assays with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers affirm these findings, with Reviewer 1 noting reduced tRNA binding and Reviewer 2 praising quantification of both activity and RNA binding. Peer review also includes additional claims (C22, C23, C26, C94) not grouped by OpenEval.

OpenEval supports oligomer formation and altered migration (C44-C46) based on EMSA data in Figure 2 supplement. Peer review groups these claims with broader functional consequences (R2), affirming the impact on RNA modification and binding but not specifically discussing oligomerization.

Both strongly support crystallographic findings (C51-C60). OpenEval emphasizes 1.9Å resolution and clear electron density for specific residue interactions. Peer reviewers praise the high-quality structure, with Reviewer 2 noting it increases confidence in protein-protein contacts and Reviewer 1 highlighting the distinct binding conformation.

Both support P3'-in/P3'-out binding mode classification (C63-C66, C115-C116). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative structural alignments and dihedral angle analysis. Peer reviewers affirm significance for drug design, with Reviewer 2 calling the two-conformation concept significant and Reviewer 1 noting fundamental importance for understanding Mpro as drug target. Peer review also includes drug design implications (C117-C119).

Both support kinetic measurements (C67-C72). OpenEval emphasizes triplicate fluorogenic assays and quantitative kinetic parameters showing TRMT1 as viable substrate. Peer reviewers affirm findings, with Reviewer 1 noting similar kinetics to nsp8/9 and Reviewer 2 praising extensive in vitro kinetic assays, though noting ideal conditions as context.

Both support mutagenesis findings (C73-C76) but note limitations. OpenEval documents lack of kinetic changes upon mutation as surprising but well-documented. Peer reviewers acknowledge the data but note it leaves questions unanswered about substrate preference, with Reviewer 2 calling this a challenging problem requiring more effort.

OpenEval groups structural observations (C73-C74) with kinetic mutagenesis data. Peer R15 treats these conformational changes as part of the high-quality crystal structure analysis supporting P3'-in binding mode, without linking to mutagenesis results.

Both support evolutionary findings (C77-C82, C21). OpenEval emphasizes sequence analysis across Muroidea and experimental validation of Q530K resistance. Peer reviewers affirm these findings, with Reviewer 1 confirming resistance to cleavage and Reviewer 2 praising the evolutionary perspective on virus-host interactions.

Both support MD simulation findings (C84-C87). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative probabilities from 100ns trajectories and consistency with crystal structures. Peer reviewers accept the findings, with Reviewer 2 noting interpretations seem reasonable and convincing despite not being able to comment on simulation rigor.

Both support conclusions about post-binding discrimination (C88-C91, C125). OpenEval emphasizes integrated analysis showing similar binding geometries cannot explain kinetic differences. Peer reviewers accept this logical inference from combined structural, kinetic, and computational data without challenge.

Perfect agreement on validation by concurrent work (C100-C101). Both cite Zhang et al., 2024 as independent validation during viral infection. Reviewer 1 notes the manuscript complements the companion article, and no reviewer questions the cited findings.

Both rate speculative claims about physiological impact as uncertain (C18, C27-C28, C104, C110-C111). OpenEval notes direct evidence is not provided and future experiments are required. Peer reviewers accept in vitro findings but note the manuscript falls short of testing functional hypotheses, leaving broader implications uncertain.

Both support drug design implications (C129, C131). OpenEval notes structural characterization is solid but therapeutic utility is hypothetical. Peer reviewers affirm significance for drug design, with Reviewer 2 stating the two-conformation concept can guide drug design and Reviewer 1 noting it will help efforts to target Mpro.

OpenEval groups drug design speculation (C118-C119) with S3' pocket observations. Peer R4 includes these claims with broader P3'-in/P3'-out binding mode findings, affirming significance for drug design without separating speculative from established structural findings.

Both support high-level conclusions about substrate recognition complexity (C126-C127). OpenEval synthesizes from multiple negative results. Peer reviewers accept these as valid contributions, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging the challenging problem and treating inability to fully explain differences as honest limitation rather than flaw.

OpenEval rates AlphaFold2 predictions (C112-C114) as uncertain due to lack of experimental validation. Peer reviewers group these with other contextual claims as supported by appropriate citations, not questioning the computational predictions but treating them as background.

OpenEval supports inference about Muroidea resistance (C83) as reasonable based on in vitro data. Peer R7 groups this with broader evolutionary findings (C77-C82), affirming the evolutionary perspective without separately evaluating the inference about resistance in infected animals.

Both support P1' substitution findings (C121-C122). OpenEval emphasizes lack of effect from Ala to Ser change as surprising but well-documented. Peer R6 groups this with broader mutagenesis results, acknowledging the data while noting it leaves substrate preference questions unanswered.

Both support negative geometric findings (C123-C124). OpenEval emphasizes these rule out simple explanations for differential cleavage rates. Peer reviewers accept as valid contributions supporting the conclusion that discrimination occurs at later catalytic steps, treating as honest limitations.

Peer reviewers support background and contextual claims (C1-C17) as well-founded by citations. OpenEval does not create a separate result for these background claims, likely treating them as established context rather than findings requiring evaluation.

Peer reviewers support additional contextual claims (C47-C48, C102-C103, C105-C109, C128, C130) from literature. OpenEval does not separately evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on primary experimental findings of the manuscript.

Peer reviewers support background claim about predicted interaction (C92) from Gordon et al., 2020b and Meyer et al., 2021. OpenEval does not separately evaluate this contextual claim, treating it as established rationale for the study.
